reflection.assumptions: Experiences of the pandemic may be shaped by health system preparedness, governance decisions, resource allocation, public health policies, and lessons carried forward from previous outbreaks such as Ebola.

coding_output:
Initial Code: Community perception of COVID-19 as a real threat  
Clues: "Corona is real and that why the precautions that the government has put in place that the whole world has put in place they said we should abide by them, it real."  
Initial Code: Traditional medicine influences healthcare decisions  
Clues: "People were having this concept that it won’t be treated by the English way unless I go for traditional native medicines that the only it could be treated..."  
Initial Code: Government lockdown impacts on daily life  
Clues: "It one of the measures that government really put in place like the face mask and all of cause it affected people especially those with asthma diseases..."  
Initial Code: School closures leading to poor academic outcomes  
Clues: "look at the results that came out because schools closed earlier then second term school was closed so the whole of third term there was no school..."  
Initial Code: Transportation challenges during lockdown  
Clues: "well there was no transportation, especially district lockdown transportation was high, and the people with money travels only..."  
Initial Code: Economic strain on daily wage earners during lockdown  
Clues: "the ones that has no chance you see them sitting down lonely observing and say how, grumbling all over like what is this?... how will they survive..."  
Initial Code: Social distancing as a preventive measure  
Clues: "social distancing is more preventable because of that saliva or the sneezes from someone that it won’t meet with you..."  
Initial Code: Challenges faced by vulnerable populations during lockdown  
Clues: "it was affecting them that one and three days that we were sitting down especially for we in the districts it was affecting us."  
Initial Code: Experience of stricter COVID-19 restrictions
Clues: "we restrict ourselves. ... the government said we should sit let us sit and for now that the government has ease on us its more better."
Initial Code: Comparison of government responses to Ebola and COVID-19
Clues: "during the time of EBOLA the restriction was there but it was not that much, and for that made people to come here because we had no experience. ... as compared to this one before it came government had blocked all the borders and all the districts."
Initial Code: Lack of social distancing and protective measures during Ebola
Clues: "no mask was available, no social distancing. ... they will come with food because they were keeping people in there for three weeks."
Initial Code: Government enforcement of COVID-19 guidelines
Clues: "yes because they enforced it, they enforced the measures, you don’t abide, and they fine a levy on you. ... they involve all the stakeholders so the fight was a national fight to the level that it would be."
Initial Code: Preparedness from previous Ebola experience 
Clues: "exactly because is just like when they say war ... the EBOLA when it came we had no idea now when the COVID is here the previous government they have already know although they still don’t have measures."
Initial Code: Quick government response to COVID-19  
Clues: "they responded quickly. ... because they attack the disease earlier."  
Initial Code: Government health centers poorly positioned  
Clues: "they were putting centers wherein the position was not there, they were creating centers for admitting people but there was no position..."  
Initial Code: Delayed salary payments to health workers  
Clues: "even the infected people at the end of the day then even the workers the soldiers that were on the forefront it reach at a time the salary time they didn’t pay them..."  
Initial Code: Availability of essential drugs in hospitals  
Clues: "government should try to improve on the health centers, more improvement on the health system especially the drugs. Let the drugs be available in the hospitals..."  
Initial Code: Poor sanitation and facilities in government hospitals  
Clues: "the toilet facility sanitation. Government hospital has no toilet facility they are there but the control measures is poor so they closed them."  
Initial Code: Increased costs of healthcare during COVID-19  
Clues: "the time when I did this operation for my hernia in 2015 it costs le 500,000 but initially when I went to the finance doctor told me go and pay to that woman, me and the doctor has discussed everything the woman went on writing thinking it was hernia and she wrote le 900,000..."  
Initial Code: Comparison of care between private and government hospitals  
Clues: "the nurses in the private hospital are more caring, the wards very lonely, very quiet like if you go there you don’t hear noise but unlike for government hospital a lot of noise."  
Initial Code: Relationship with healthcare providers enhances care  
Clues: "I will make sure I have a good relation. So me and doctor [retracted] has had that good relations, I took his number and we have been communicating day and night..."  
Initial Code: Impact of past Ebola experience on current healthcare perception  
Clues: "I was just been relieved from the EBOLA, there was no caring."  
Initial Code: Government communication regarding COVID-19  
Clues: "government announces it, so they have given their own measures so we that has the responsibilities we the citizens."  
Initial Code: Perception of unequal resource allocation
Clues: "they should put more premium on them but surgical they should also put premium they should care for us because if they do not care where they do the operation it could reoccur so if you are not careful you will die so they should care for us more. ... because we see they provide donor for them, they pour more money on COVID but we never saw donor for operation."
Initial Code: Concerns about timely access to medication
Clues: "they should improve on the monitoring not only the buildings like all the facilities more especially the drugs should be available in the hospitals. When you need when they write your prescription you go down and buy quickly and come and go. By the time you ran to town to go and buy drugs and come you will meet the patients have collapse."
Initial Code: Need for better healthcare infrastructure
Clues: "let them improve on it the light system in the hospital should be okay. ... they should improve on the monitoring not only the buildings like all the facilities more especially the drugs should be available in the hospitals."
Initial Code: Support for additional resources for COVID care
Clues: "Yes ... because it contagious, it a thing that transfer if you are not careful and how many workers did it kill I think it 2 the one doctor I think he was lecturing and the one is here so therefore we were arguing and arguing."
Initial Code: Recommendations for vaccination strategies
Clues: "if there is a vaccine that they will inject a person for him not to have that diseases that what they should be fighting for let say an Anti-drug, take the drug and it will be in your system for years so that even if the outbreak comes you won’t get infected."
Initial Code: Fear of seeking care during the pandemic
Clues: "people were having other diseases which is not EBOLA but they are afraid to go to the hospital."
